title: PHP2Shell Makes PHP Inventory and Patch Ownership Urgent
content_md: TL;DR PHP2Shell is the name being used for two critical PHP vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 . Both can allow unauthenticated remote code execution. PHP says all PHP installations serving web requests are at risk, with the highest risk in Apache configurations using mod_php. Fixed releases are PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35. Organizations should inventory PHP across their environments, prioritize internet-facing systems, monitor for suspicious activity, and apply the update through PHP or the relevant distribution or product vendor. If a system cannot be remediated promptly, consider taking it offline until it is fully mitigated. PHP2Shell Is Two Critical Flaws in the PHP Runtime PHP2Shell refers to two vulnerabilities in PHP's internal request handling. Because PHP is used in websites, applications, and products, affected installations may be managed by different teams or supplied through different vendors.The urgent work is to find those systems, establish who owns each one, and verify that the fix reaches every deployment.
